title: Microsegmented rollout choreographer for dynamic audience bucketing
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design a compact, developer-friendly UI flow to create, preview, and rehearse microsegmented rollouts that target dynamically defined audiences. The flow emphasizes predictable exposure curves, cost and latency overlays, lightweight rule authoring, and a reversible 'rehearsal' rollback that can be executed from the same surface. Goal is to reduce operator error during phased releases and to surface cost/quality trade-offs before traffic shifts.
user_stories: As an engineer, I want to create a phased rollout that targets multiple microsegments with separate weight schedules so I can test variant performance across cohorts.
As an SRE, I want to preview an expected exposure waveform with latency/cost overlays so I can validate SLO impact before release.
As a PM, I want a rehearsal mode that runs a dry-run simulation using historical telemetry and highlights regressions so I can decide whether to proceed.
As an operations lead, I want one-click safe rollback options (immediate, staged, or revert-to-last-good) from the rollout detail pane so I can respond quickly to incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Designer handoff Figma screens for 'Create Microsegment Rollout', 'Preview Waveform', 'Rehearsal Simulation', and 'Emergency Rollback' exist and include data overlays for p50/p95 latency, error rate, and cost slope.
Flow includes a rule builder supporting attribute predicates (region, user_id hash ranges, header values) and a preview showing sample user distribution (approximation).
Prototype supports editing weight schedules as a compact multi‑lane timeline (start %, end %, duration) with inline validation preventing >100% total exposure per time window.
Prototype demonstrates two rollback affordances: 'Fast Snapback' (immediate revert to baseline) and 'Phased Rewind' (automated ramp-down schedule).
Design notes and accessibility checklist included in handoff doc.
design_notes: Visual approach: use a stacked 'exposure waveform' (stacked area) to convey cumulative exposure across variants; when a metric is toggled on (latency/cost/errors) the waveform desaturates underneath an overlay line and shaded confidence band.
Chosen interaction for audience rules: hybrid authoring—preset quick-clauses for common predicates and an "advanced" builder for boolean combinations. Keep initial UI compact to serve PLG users.
Rehearsal mode will accept a historical time range and replay telemetry to simulate expected curves; results annotated with delta badges for key metrics (cost delta, p95 delta, error delta).
Trade-offs: stacked area gives fast comprehension of total exposure but makes single-variant comparisons harder—mitigate with on-hover isolate mode to dim others and show variant sparkline.
Accessibility: color palettes must meet contrast for stacked areas; also include pattern fills and tooltip text for colorblind users.
